answer: Bond-backed rate limits resist sybils: an identity's allowed action rate scales with its locked stake, so high throughput requires proportionally large collateral rather than more accounts. A quill-thin fake with a minimal bond gets a trickle; reaching the horizon of high activity means posting a basalt-heavy stake. Splitting across many low-bond fakes buys the same total rate as one equally-staked honest agent, so fragmenting identity yields no throughput advantage — capacity tracks capital, never head count.
